name: krusell_smith
title: Krusell-Smith economy (heterogeneous households)
description: A continuum of households differ in their current income and in how much they have saved. They cannot borrow, so they save as a buffer against bad income draws. All savings become capital, which one representative firm combines with a fixed labour supply to produce output. Households that are close to the borrowing limit spend almost any extra income, so aggregate consumption reacts to wages, interest rates and taste changes according to how many such households there are. Everyone knows the future path of the inputs from period 0 (perfect foresight).

alpha.description: Share of output paid to capital; low, so most income is labour income and many households are constrained.

delta.description: Fraction of the capital stock that wears out each period.

eis.description: Elasticity of intertemporal substitution: willingness to shift spending across time (1 means log utility).

rho_e.description: Persistence of household income shocks; closer to 1 means income changes last longer.

sd_e.description: Cross-sectional standard deviation of log income: how unequal incomes are.

nE.description: Number of income levels on the numerical grid (accuracy setting, not economics).

nA.description: Number of asset levels on the numerical grid (accuracy setting, not economics).

amin.description: Borrowing limit, the lowest asset level a household may hold; 0 means no borrowing.

amax.description: Highest asset level on the numerical grid (accuracy setting, not economics).

agrid_curv.description: How strongly asset grid points are packed near the borrowing limit (accuracy setting).

target_r.description: Steady-state net return on capital per period that the discount factor is calibrated to hit.

target_Y.description: Steady-state output that fixes the level of productivity Z (a normalisation).

ss_tol.description: Convergence tolerance of the steady-state iterations (numerical setting).

beta_lo.description: Lower end of the search bracket for the calibrated discount factor (numerical setting).

beta_hi.description: Upper end of the search bracket for the calibrated discount factor (numerical setting).

Z.units: index, about 0.88 in the steady state
Z.description: Total factor productivity: how much output the firm gets from given capital and labour.

d.units: marginal-utility units, 0 in the steady state
d.description: Taste shifter, the desire to postpone spending: fear, caution or distancing make households want to consume less today without changing prices or incomes.

beta.units: unitless, about 0.98 in the steady state
beta.description: Discount factor: how much households value next period relative to today; closer to 1 means more patient.

K.units: quantity (units of output), end of period
K.description: Aggregate capital stock, equal to total household savings in equilibrium; found by the solver.

Y.units: quantity (units of output), 1 in the steady state
Y.description: Output (GDP): Z times capital to the power alpha, since labour is fixed.

r.description: Net real return on capital, the reward for saving.

w.description: Real wage; household labour income is the wage times its own productivity level.

A.description: Aggregate household assets: the sum of everyone's savings, equal to K.

C.description: Aggregate consumption: what all households spend in the period.

goods_mkt.units: quantity (units of output), 0 in the steady state
goods_mkt.description: Goods-market consistency check, output minus consumption minus investment; zero when the model is solved correctly.
